sections.text: A Snapshot keeps what the dashboard showed for one week, month, quarter, half-year or year (quarters, half-years and years of the Workspace's fiscal year, such as "Q1 FY 2026/27" when the year starts in April, or "H2 2026" and "2026" when it starts in January): its layout and the values of every Metric period complete by the period's last day. Its values never change, even when someone corrects one later. Its words (the introduction and each Finding's headline and lines) you write afterwards, such as "What happened in October".

sections.heading: The Snapshots menu
sections.text:
Snapshots in the toolbar lists the dashboard's Snapshots, newest period first (of periods that end on the same day, the longer first: "2026", "H2 2026", "Q4 2026", "December 2026"), under "The dashboard as it stood for a period". A Snapshot still in draft is marked Draft. Choose one to open it.
The owner and Editors also see:
Take a Snapshot… (not Guests).
For the owner only: Take one by itself…, or Takes one every month… once set (see Automatic Snapshots).

sections.heading: Taking a Snapshot
sections.text:
Take a Snapshot… asks:
Period: Month, Quarter, Half-year, Year or Week.
Which: one of the last complete periods, the most recent first. Only a period that is over can be taken.
Press Take Snapshot. Ziffr keeps the dashboard as it is now, with the values up to the end of that period, and opens the Snapshot so you can write it up. To take one, you must see every Metric on the dashboard. A dashboard has at most one Snapshot per period, at most 500 in all, going back at most ten years.

sections.heading: Reading and writing a Snapshot
sections.text:
A band at the top of a Snapshot says which period it is, when and by whom it was taken ("by Ziffr for" the owner when it was taken automatically), and Draft: only the dashboard's owner and Editors see it while it is a draft. See it live goes to the dashboard as it is today. Below, the dashboard reads top to bottom, drawn from the values it kept.
If you may not see some of its Metrics, the band says how many parts are not shown.
If a value was corrected or removed since, the band lists it under "Corrected since this Snapshot was taken; it keeps the values it had", with the value then and what…

sections.heading: Example: the annual review
sections.text:
A dashboard "Annual review" shows Revenue by month. In January 2027 its owner opens Snapshots ▸ Take a Snapshot…, chooses Year and 2026, and presses Take Snapshot. The Snapshot "2026" keeps Revenue's twelve months of 2026 and those before, not January 2027. The owner writes the introduction ("Revenue grew by a quarter; the second half carried it") and shows it. In the Snapshots menu it comes first, above "H2 2026", "Q4 2026" and "December 2026". Make a deck on it starts the deck "Annual review, 2026" for the board.
To have it taken by itself next year, choose Take one by itself… ▸ Every year.…

sections.heading: Sent by a Workflow
sections.text: A Workflow can take, show and send a dashboard's Snapshot too, with its Send Snapshot step (see Workflows and approvals): once the Workflow's period is finished, it takes the period's Snapshot in the Workflow owner's name (the owner must still own or edit the dashboard and see every Metric on it), shows it, and sends the people it names, who may open the dashboard, a link to it. The Audit Log says the Snapshot was taken and shown "via workflow". The message carries no value; whoever opens the link sees only the Metrics they may see.

sections.heading: Automatic Snapshots
sections.text:
The dashboard's owner can have it take a Snapshot by itself. Choose Take one by itself…:
Take one: Only by hand, Every month, Every quarter, Every half-year, Every year or Every week.
Wait at most (days): from 0 to 60, 5 by default.
Each period's Snapshot is then taken in the owner's name as soon as every Metric on the dashboard is Locked for every one of its periods in it (for a year of a monthly Metric, all twelve months), or that many days after the period ends, whichever comes first. Ziffr tells the owner it is ready to write up. It stays a draft until someone shows it. A Snapshot deleted…

sections.heading: Versions
sections.text:
A Version is a saved state of something you build, with who made it and when. Dashboards, single Widgets, team Widget Templates, Decks and a Snapshot's words all keep Versions. Edits by one person within ten minutes form one Version.
Versions opens a panel on the right with the list, newest first. Each shows its number (such as "v12"), its name or "Current" or "Edited", who made it and when, and what changed.
If you may change the thing (its owner and Editors), you also see:
Name this state and Save: names the current state, such as "Board pack Q3, final", so you can find it again.
Name /…

sections.heading: Old story addresses
sections.text: Earlier, Ziffr had stories as a screen of their own. They are now dashboards with an introduction, read in the Read view. An old address of a story opens that dashboard in its Read view, and the old stories list opens the Dashboards list.

sections.heading: Panels have their own address
sections.text: Share, Who can see this, View links, Versions and a Metric's quick look open as panels on the right, over the page; on a phone they fill the screen. The address of the page then ends in ?panel=share (Who can see this and View links have no address of their own: they open from Share or the ⋯ menu, and Back in the panel returns to Share), ?panel=versions or ?panel=metric- and the Metric's short name, so you can send the link and whoever opens it sees the page with the panel open. While a panel is open the keys stay inside it; Esc or Close closes it and puts you back where you were.

sections.heading: Analyze
sections.text:
Analyze in the sidebar opens the Analysis Canvas: a place to put a few Metrics side by side and ask simple questions of them. Where is this heading? Do these two move together? What moves Cost? You choose a method by what you want to know, and its result can go onto a dashboard.
Everyone in the Workspace can use Analyze, with the Metrics they can see. The page needs no setup and changes nothing for anyone else.

sections.heading: The screen
sections.text:
The screen has three parts:
The Pool on the left (below on a narrow screen), with the Metrics you can see. Here it holds only Metrics, no saved Widgets or Widget Templates. Filter narrows it by name.
Choose a method at the top: the one way to run an analysis here. It is a list of questions grouped by what you want to know (see Choose a method). On an empty canvas the list is already open.
The Analysis canvas, with the Metrics on it and which of them is the one to explain.

sections.heading: Putting Metrics on the canvas
sections.text: Drag a Metric from the Pool onto the canvas, or point at it and press +. Archived Metrics are not in the Pool, and the Drivers suggestion leaves them out. To see what a Metric is before you drop it, press the ⓘ on its row: a small card opens beside it with the Metric's name, how often it is counted and in which unit, its description, its latest value with the period, and a small line of its recent values. The list stays as it is; press ⓘ again, press Escape or tap elsewhere to close the card. You can also open a Metric's own page and choose Analyze there: Ziffr opens this screen with that…

sections.heading: The Metric to explain
sections.text:
Some questions are about one Metric: What moves B?, What does B need to reach a value?, What if A changes? and Did it work?. Ziffr calls it the one to explain. When there are two or more Metrics on the canvas, each chip says its role in words: the one to explain carries a filled mark, The one to explain, and the others read Compared with and have a button, Make this the one to explain. The mark is its own choice: the order in which you dropped the Metrics does not decide it. With one Metric on the canvas, it is the one to explain.
Choose another Metric's button and nothing is taken off the…

sections.heading: Choose a method
sections.text:
Choose a method, at the top of the screen, is the one way to run an analysis: it is for when you know what you want to know and not which Method gives it. It opens a list grouped by the question: Where is it heading?, What moves with what?, What would it take?, What would happen if?, What changed?, What is usual? and Where is it concentrated?. Each entry has its plain name ("Does A move with B?"), the technical name in small type after it, one sentence of what it tells you, and Use it when / Don't use it when under it, the same words as the Methods guide.
The list fits the canvas, and what…

sections.heading: Did it work?
sections.text:
Pick Did it work? or Did something change, and when? from What changed? in Choose a method. 
The answer is a range, not a verdict: "After 1 Mar 2026, Signups ran about 12.0 % above where its trend pointed (likely between +8.1 % and +16.2 %; that range leaves out zero)." The trend is a straight line through the periods before the day you named, so Ziffr needs at least six of them; the latest 120 are used, and the first 120 periods since the day. A period that began before the day and runs past it is left out, and the result says so. "Likely between" is the range the answer holds about four…

sections.heading: Heads-ups
sections.text:
At the top of Analyze, a list called Heads-ups shows what Ziffr noticed in the Metrics you can see, without being asked. There are five kinds:
Two Metrics have started moving together ("A and B have started moving together: when A rises, B follows one month later (strong, over 18 months)"), or used to and have stopped ("A and B used to move together. Over the last 6 months, they have not.").
A Metric turned around ("Signups turned around in January 2026: up 3 a month before, down 9 a month since").
A Target looks out of reach ("Revenue is unlikely to reach 1,500 € or more in January 2027…

sections.heading: Reading the results
sections.text: The Analyses Forecast, Correlation, Drivers and Correlation matrix are also Widgets, which you place on a dashboard from the Analyses group of the Pool; the results of Choose a method say the same things in a Takeaway. A Widget has a title saying what it compares, such as "Forecast: Revenue", "Return rate vs. Support tickets", "Drivers of Cost" or "Correlation matrix (5 metrics)".

sections.heading: Forecast
sections.text:
A line of the Metric's last 18 periods, continued a few periods ahead: two quarters for a quarterly Metric, one year for a yearly one, three months for a monthly Metric, six weeks for a weekly one, fourteen days for a daily one. A shaded band around the continued line shows how far the actual values will likely be from it; it widens the further ahead it looks. Above the line, one sentence sums it up, such as "Expected €1.2M by June 2027 (likely €1.0M–€1.4M)".
The forecast follows the recent trend of the values. It knows nothing of plans, seasons or events, so read it as "where this is heading…

sections.heading: Correlation
sections.text:
A dot for each period, placed by the two Metrics' values, and a Takeaway behind the Widget's ⋯ menu (Takeaway…): one sentence in the Metrics' own words, such as "Visits and Revenue tend to move together over 18 months (strong)."
The word in brackets says how clear the link is: strong, moderate, weak, or can't tell from chance. The last one means the pattern is no clearer than what luck alone could give, so do not lean on it. Read more in Reading a Takeaway.
Above the sentence, a plain line appears when something about the data makes the reading rough: a few periods far from the rest that pull…

sections.heading: Metrics counted at different periods
sections.text:
Two Metrics counted at different periods, such as weekly support tickets and monthly churn, are compared on the longer of the two, their Common Period. The shorter one is combined by its Aggregation (see Metrics): weekly tickets are added up to monthly tickets, an average is averaged, a last value is taken from the period's last week. A daily Metric against a weekly one is compared by week, and so on.
Only complete periods count. The month still running is left out, as it would compare part of a month with whole ones.
The result says so under the sentence: "Compared by month (18 months)".…

sections.heading: Drivers
sections.text: A list of the other Metrics, the one that moves most closely with the one to explain first. Each has a bar for how strong the link is and its link number, r (from −1 to 1; the further from 0, the closer the two move together). A bar in the data colour means they move the same way; a bar in the warning colour means they move opposite ways. Below the list, a Takeaway names up to three that moved with the one to explain the most ("Over 18 months, Shipping cost and Returns moved with Cost the most.") and a dot chart shows the two. Each Metric in the list has its own Takeaway behind Show the…

sections.heading: Correlation matrix
sections.text: A grid with every Metric on both sides. Each square holds the link number r of that pair. The stronger the link, the deeper its colour; pairs that move opposite ways are shaded in the warning colour. A pair counted at different periods (monthly against weekly) is compared on the longer one. Pointing at a square shows its link number, whether growth was removed ("Compared by change, growth removed" or "Compared by value") and, for such a pair, "Compared by month (18 months)". A pair with no result shows "–", and pointing at it says why, such as "Not enough months in common (4 of 6)." Below the…

sections.heading: View Designs
sections.text:
View Designs at the top right of Analyze opens the list of designs. A View Design is a View written as a file: which Metrics it takes, what it draws and in which Theme colours. It holds no code. Ziffr checks the file and draws it with its own renderer, and every number in it is one Ziffr computes.
The Workspace's View Designs: the designs Owners and Admins added. Everyone in the Workspace finds them in the Pool, under The Workspace's View Designs, and places them like a built-in View.
Built-in View Designs: every built-in View and Analysis, drawn with Sample Data.
Export downloads the…

sections.heading: Playground
sections.text:
Playground at the top right of Analyze is where you work on a View Design's file. The file is on the left, the drawing on the right.
Start from loads a built-in View's design; Upload loads a file. You can also paste or type.
The file is in a code editor with colours. While you type, it offers the fields and values the format allows at the cursor (press Ctrl+Space to ask for them) and says what a field means when you rest the pointer on it or its value. The editor does not take the Tab key, so Tab moves on to the next control. If the editor cannot load, the file stays a plain text box. How to…

sections.heading: Analysis Recipes
sections.text: An Analysis Recipe is an Analysis written as steps of Ziffr's own functions: moving average, difference, growth, share, linear trend and slope, mean, standard deviation, z-score, seasonal index and correlation. A View Design can carry one under analysis and draw its results: as a line or bars (recipe. and the step's name), as a rule across a plot for one value, or as a number in its words. The recipe works on the Metrics in the design's first Slots, as the Widget shows them (by quarter, when it is shown by quarter), and on nothing else. Every number it gives is computed by Ziffr's verified…

sections.heading: Saving a result
sections.text:
Results are not kept when you leave the screen; save the ones you want. A result of Choose a method has Save as widget under it (see above). A Widget on a dashboard has a ⋯ menu, which right-clicking also opens:
A result placed on a dashboard keeps working there: it is drawn again from the latest values each time the dashboard opens. You can also place an Analysis on a dashboard directly, from the Analyses group of Widget Templates in the dashboard's Pool. See Dashboards and Findings.

sections.heading: Decks and Themes
sections.text:
A Deck is a set of slides you build from your Widgets, text, arrows and shapes. You can present it in Ziffr, or export it as PowerPoint or PDF for a board meeting. A Theme decides how your dashboards and decks look: colours, fonts, cards and what every slide shows.
Open Decks in the sidebar. Owners, Admins and Members can make decks. Guests only see decks that someone shared with them: they get no New deck and no Themes link, and an empty list says "Nothing has been shared with you yet. Ask whoever invited you." The Themes page opens from the Themes link on the Decks page, or next to the…

sections.heading: The Decks page
sections.text:
The page lists every deck you made and every deck someone shared with you. Each card shows the deck's name, how many slides it has and when it was last changed. On a deck from someone else, the card also says who it is from and what you may do: "you can edit it" or "you can present it".
Open a deck by choosing its card. If you may change it, the deck opens in the editor. If you may only present it, it opens for presenting.
Make a new deck: type a name in Name of the new deck and choose New deck. The deck opens in the editor and starts with one title slide.
Make a deck from a Deck Template:…

sections.heading: The deck editor
sections.text:
A deck that came in with a Workspace Export starts empty. The first time you open it, the editor lays out its slides from today's values, as for a deck made from a Deck Template, and saves them.
The editor has three parts: a row of buttons at the top, a side panel on the left, and the deck canvas, where your slides sit.
Changes save by themselves a moment after you make them. Next to the deck's name you see Saved, Saving… or Unsaved changes. To rename the deck, click its name at the top and type. On a narrow screen the buttons move to a second line before the name is cut short.
The panel of…

sections.heading: The buttons at the top
sections.text:
The ⋯ menu holds:
Group and Ungroup are in the side panel, in a box that shows while something selected can be grouped or ungrouped. They keep several selected things on one slide together, or split a group again. Only things on the same slide can be grouped. The shortcuts are Ctrl+G and Ctrl+Shift+G (⌘G and ⌘Shift+G on a Mac).

sections.heading: Slide layouts
sections.text:
Slide offers these layouts. Each one only places starting text, which you can change or delete.
Below them, under Team layouts, you find slides that people in your team saved (see Saving a slide as a layout). Each shows who made it. If a team layout has Slots, Ziffr first asks which Metrics should fill them. Its words are then filled in from today's data.

sections.heading: Slides and their order
sections.text:
A Slide is one 16:9 page of the deck. New slides go below the last one. You can drag slides around on the canvas like any other object.
The order of the slides is their position on the canvas: left to right, then top to bottom. That order is used when you present, when you export and for the slide numbers. To move a slide earlier, drag it above or to the left of the slide it should come before.

sections.heading: Adding Widgets
sections.text:
The Pool on the left holds the Metrics you can see, your saved Widgets and the Widget Templates. Drag one onto a slide, or choose + next to it to add it to the slide you are looking at. It lands in the first free space on that slide, next to what is already there; if the slide is full, it is made smaller to fit.
A Metric dropped on a slide becomes a line chart. You can change that afterwards.
A Widget Template asks for its Metrics first.
A Widget shows live numbers: whenever a new value arrives, the slide shows it.
You can only place Metrics you may see. Everyone you share the deck with can…

sections.heading: Text, arrows, shapes and images
sections.text:
The toolbar at the bottom of the canvas has the tools for text, arrows, lines, shapes, sticky notes and free drawing. Text and lines start in plain type with solid lines.
You can paste or drop an image file onto a slide. Links cannot go on a slide: Ziffr shows "Links can't go on a slide", because a link would load from another site every time the slide is shown. Paste or drop the image itself instead.

sections.heading: The side panel
sections.text:
What the side panel shows depends on what you have selected.
A Widget selected. The Visualization list changes how the Widget draws its Metric, with the same choices as on a dashboard. The note below it reminds you which ones become editable charts in PowerPoint. A Widget drawn by one of the Workspace's View Designs keeps its design on the slide, titled by the design's name when it is an Analysis. When the Widget is a Finding, its editor opens below, so you can change its headline, words and panels.
A slide selected. Click the edge or the name of a slide to select it.
Always shown: Footer on…

sections.heading: Saving a slide as a layout
sections.text: Select a slide and choose Save slide as layout…; a panel opens beside the slide. Give it a name and, if you like, a description. The Metrics on the slide become Slots, so others can fill the layout with their own Metrics. Everyone in the team can use the layout from + Slide, under Team layouts. Only you can change it.

sections.heading: Saving a deck as a Deck Template
sections.text: A Deck Template keeps a whole deck: every slide with its Widgets, words and boxes, with the Metrics left open as Slots. Choose Save as Deck Template… at the top; a panel opens beside the deck. A Metric shown on several slides becomes one Slot, which you can name, such as "Revenue". Its name in the words becomes {metric}. Notes tied to one period or row can follow a rule instead, or are left out, as for a layout. Images and links stay behind. You can do this for a deck of your own once it is saved, when you see every Metric on it. Everyone in the team can then start a deck from it on the Decks…

sections.heading: Presenting
sections.text:
Choose Present to show the deck one slide at a time, filling the screen, with live numbers. Nobody can change the deck while it is presented.
Next slide: the right arrow, down arrow, Page Down or the space bar, a click on the right part of the slide, a swipe, or › at the bottom.
Previous slide: the left arrow, up arrow, Page Up, a click on the left part of the slide, a swipe, or ‹.
First and last slide: Home and End.
Full screen: the button at the bottom right. Stop presenting (the ×) or Escape takes you back to the editor.
The bar at the bottom shows the deck's name and which slide you are…

sections.heading: Exporting to PowerPoint and PDF
sections.text:
An exported deck is a Snapshot: it holds the values its Widgets show at the moment you export. Every slide carries the stamp "Data as of" and that day's date, so readers know how old the numbers are. The deck in Ziffr stays live.
Slides are exported in their order on the canvas. Each export is noted in the workspace's Audit Log.
Widgets in a deck that show condensed periods (see Dashboards, Show by) draw them as the app does, with points such as "October 2023, condensed from 31 days"; a Snapshot or deck keeps what it showed.

sections.heading: Export PowerPoint
sections.text:
Choose Export PowerPoint. Your browser downloads a file named after the deck.
Text, shapes and arrows become normal PowerPoint objects you can edit.
Line and bar Widgets, and Findings with ranked bars, become real PowerPoint charts you can edit. Their values are rounded to the Metric's decimals the way Ziffr shows them: 1.005 at two decimals is 1.01.
Number Widgets become text, and history tables become tables. Values are written as in Ziffr, in the Workspace's Number Style with the Metric's unit. Under the value stands the Widget's first comparison, exactly as the Widget shows it, such as…

sections.heading: PDF
sections.text:
Choose PDF. Ziffr opens the deck in a new browser tab and starts printing. Choose "Save as PDF" in the print window to keep a file. Each page shows "Data as of", the date and the slide number. If nothing opens, allow pop-ups for Ziffr in your browser.
If an export fails, Ziffr says "Export failed". Try again, or remove the last thing you added.

sections.heading: Sharing a deck
sections.text:
Sharing a deck works like sharing a dashboard. Dashboards and Findings explains Shares, View Links and Versions in full. In short:
Share gives people or Groups a role on the deck. A Viewer can present it. An Editor can also change its slides, name, footer and Theme. Only the owner shares the deck and makes View Links.
Invite someone… at the bottom of the Share panel invites a person who is not in the Workspace yet, by email, as Member or Guest; only Owners and Admins see it, others are told "Ask an Owner or Admin to invite them".
View link lets someone outside the team watch the deck slide by…

sections.heading: The Themes page
sections.text:
The page shows every Theme of the Workspace on the left. The one marked team default is used everywhere a dashboard or deck has not picked another. Choose a theme to see and change it.
Below your Themes, Standard Themes lists the six that come with Ziffr: Ziffr Light, Ziffr Dark, Tokyo (dark, vivid colours), Paris (warm, serif headlines), Oslo (cool and restrained) and Print (black on white, for PDF and PowerPoint). Choose one to see it on real Widgets, then Add to this Workspace: it becomes a Theme of your own, which you can pick for dashboards and decks and change like any other. Every…

sections.heading: Outside the app
sections.text:
The team default Theme also dresses what Ziffr sends and shows outside the app (it is not the same as a person's Appearance, which only changes Ziffr's own screens):
Emails (Prompts, reminders, Alerts, invitations, the usage digest, Share Proposals) get the Theme's logo or the Workspace's name, a bar in its accent, its footer and its fonts, in a layout that stays readable when the reader's mail app is dark. Only a PNG or JPEG logo of up to about 150 KB is attached; for any other, the Workspace's name stands in its place. The plain text is always sent too. The brand never replaces Ziffr's own…

sections.heading: In a dark Appearance
sections.text:
When someone's Appearance is dark, dashboards and decks in a Theme can go dark with it. The setting In a dark Appearance (under the Cards option) decides:
Every Theme has a dark variant. The Standard Themes carry one that was designed with them (Ziffr Dark and Tokyo are dark already and look the same in every Appearance). For any other Theme, Ziffr works out a dark variant from its colours and checks it for contrast (WCAG AA); if that fails, the colours of Ziffr Dark are used. The note under the setting says which one a Theme has. Fonts, corners and cards stay as they are.
Snapshots, View…

sections.heading: Fonts and cards
sections.text: The fonts to choose from are General Sans, Inter, IBM Plex Sans, Libre Franklin, Source Serif, Playfair Display, Georgia, Arial, Geist Mono and IBM Plex Mono.

sections.heading: Slides
sections.text:
These settings decide what every slide of a deck in this theme shows. A slide can hide them with Hide logo, footer and number on this slide, and a deck can set its own footer.
The type sizes apply to new slides you add. Slides that already exist keep the size their text has.

sections.heading: Saving and managing themes
sections.text:
Only Owners and Admins see Save theme, Make team default, Duplicate, Delete, Add to this Workspace and Import a Theme file. A Workspace keeps at most 50 Themes. How to write a Theme file by hand, and how to share Themes as a Pack, is in the Themes guide.
Ziffr's own screens, such as menus, settings and this guide, keep their look whatever theme you pick; they follow your Appearance.

sections.heading: Picking a theme for a dashboard or deck
sections.text:
Every dashboard and deck has a theme picker, shown with a palette icon. The first choice is the team default, shown with its name and "(team default)". A dashboard or deck on that choice follows the team default, even when the default changes later. Any other choice sticks to that one theme.
Whoever may change the dashboard or deck may pick its theme: its owner and its Editors. Viewers see it in the theme that was picked. The Themes link next to the picker opens the Themes page.

sections.heading: Actions and Changes
sections.text:
When a number looks odd, ask the person who knows. An Action is a question or a job about one value of a Metric, which one person gives to another. It is either a Question, done once it is answered, or a Task, done once someone has carried it out. The person it is given to is the Assignee. The replies about it form its Thread, and the answer stays with the value for anyone who looks later.
Everyone in the Workspace works with Actions, Guests included. This chapter also covers the Changes page, which shows what changed and when.

sections.heading: Checklist Tasks
sections.text:
A Workflow can have checklist items to tick off (see Workflows). Each period such an item gives its Assignee a Checklist Task: a Task about the Workflow and its period, such as "Reconcile the bank account", with a Due Date counted in working days after the period ends. It has no Metric, so it shows the Workflow's name and the period (such as "Month-end close, March 2026") where a Metric's name would be, and there is no chart or value on its page.
It is in the Assignee's To do view and calendar like any Task. While the Assignee is Away, it goes to the item's Stand-in instead; the Thread says…

sections.heading: The Actions row
sections.text: Schedule in the sidebar holds your Actions. Its To do view lists the Questions and Tasks given to you among the other things waiting for you; Asked by me lists the ones you asked. The number next to Schedule counts the values due and the Actions waiting for you to close. The old address of the Actions page, /actions, opens Asked by me.

sections.heading: Share Proposals: sharing an assistant prepared
sections.text:
When you ask an assistant connected to Ziffr to share numbers ("share the coffee results for the last 4 weeks with jenny@example.com"), it can only prepare the sharing. Nothing is shared and nothing is sent until you confirm it yourself in Ziffr.
A Share Proposal appears at the top of the Schedule's To do view under Waiting for your confirmation, and in the assistant's answer as a link. It says which of your dashboards, to whom and how: a View Link to an email address (with the day it ends, and the message, exactly as it would go out) or a Share to a person or Group in your Workspace. Open it…

sections.heading: Asking a Question or giving a Task
From a Widget
sections.text:
Every Widget that shows a Metric has the choices Ask a question… and Assign a task…. You find them in the Widget's ⋯ menu, or by right-clicking the Widget. This works on dashboards and wherever else a Widget shows its menu.
To ask about one value straight away, right-click that point or bar in the chart. To ask about one row of a Breakdown, such as France, right-click that row. The form then starts with that period or row filled in.
The form has these options:
Choose Send question or Assign task. Ziffr says who it was sent to and offers Open thread.

sections.heading: From a Metric's page
sections.text:
On a Metric's page, click a point in the chart ("Click a point to ask someone about it"). A small form appears with Assign to, a drafted question and Assign Action. This always makes a Question about that period. For a Task, a Due Date or a limited Thread, use a Widget's menu instead.
The chart on a Metric's page marks the periods that already have Actions, so others can see a value was asked about.

sections.heading: Who can ask
sections.text: Anyone who can see a Metric can ask about it or give a Task on it, Guests and Viewers included. The Assignee must be a person in the same Workspace.

sections.heading: Who can read an Action
sections.text:
The asker, the Assignee and the Metric's Owner can always read an Action and its Thread. Anyone else can read it only if they see its Metric, through a Share or a dashboard or deck shared with them; being an Owner or Admin of the Workspace is not enough. Of those, everyone can read it, unless the asker chose a Group under Who can read. Then only the members of that Group who see the Metric can read it, besides those three people. This holds for the Tasks a Workflow makes too, such as Approvals.
A Checklist Task has no Metric to see, so a different rule decides who reads it: the people on it…

sections.heading: The Schedule views
sections.text: The Schedule has three views, switched at the top. They show only what you may see: an Action only if you may read its Thread, and an event only about a Metric you see.

sections.heading: To do
sections.text: The default. It lists what you have to do, overdue first and then by Due Date: values to submit, Approvals waiting for you, and the Tasks and Questions given to you. See My schedule and your calendar. Values, Approvals, Tasks and Questions above the list narrow it to one kind. Above the list, To close shows the Actions you asked that were answered or done, so you can close them; they count in the number next to Schedule.

sections.heading: Asked by me
sections.text:
The Questions and Tasks you asked, in three groups, each with its count:
Each row shows:
its status: Open, Answered, Done (for a Task) or Closed,
Task and its Due Date, for a Task,
the Metric and the period, then the question or task,
the value of the period and how it changed against the period before ("150, up 50 %"), only for a Metric you see,
who asked whom, and how long ago.
Choose a row to open the Action. The newest Action comes first.

sections.heading: Timeline
sections.text:
The Timeline lists what happened, newest first, grouped by day, one line per event with its time and a dot. It is made of the Period Timelines of your Workflows (who was asked and reminded, values that came in, Approvals, publishing, locking and Snapshots) and of the Questions and Tasks on Metrics that no Workflow asks for. A line names its Workflow and period.
A line that needs attention, such as an Approval still waiting, says Needs attention in words as well as with a red dot. A finished one, such as a locked period or a Snapshot that is ready, has a tick as well as a green dot. All other…

sections.heading: What the Action shows
sections.text: At the top you see the status, whether it is a Question or Task, the Due Date, the Metric (a link to its page), the period, the Breakdown row if there is one, and the value, written in the Workspace's Number Style with the Metric's unit. If the value was corrected, the old value is shown crossed out next to it. Below that is who asked whom and when, the question or task itself, and a small chart around the period with the period marked. If you are on the Action but do not see its Metric, for example as an Approver it was never shared with, you see the Action and its value, but the Metric's…

sections.heading: Replying
sections.text:
The Thread lists every reply, oldest first, with who wrote it and when.
Only the asker, the Assignee and the Metric Owner can reply. Everyone else who may read the Action only reads.

sections.heading: Approving a value
sections.text: On an Approval waiting for you, the Action shows the value, its period, the period before it with the change, and who submitted it, with three buttons. Approve accepts the value. Send back asks what the submitter should check and returns it with your reason. Correct the value takes a number and an optional reason and proposes it as a Correction; the Metric's Owner accepts it, and the new value is approved again. You cannot approve your own value, nor a value you entered for someone, nor one entered for you (see Filling in a value for someone), and only the Approver named on the Action sees…

sections.heading: From open to closed
sections.text:
An Action moves like this:
1. Open: just asked.
2. Answered: the Assignee replied. For a Task, Done: the Assignee chose Mark done.
3. Closed: the asker closed it. The asker can close it at any time, also before an answer arrives.
When an Action is closed, the page says "Closed." and nobody can reply. The asker sees Reopen, which makes it open again.

sections.heading: Corrections
sections.text:
A Correction is a new value for the period, proposed in the Thread. Type it under Propose a correction (on a phone, the keyboard shows numbers), with a reply saying why, and choose Reply. You can leave the reply empty; Ziffr then writes "Proposing a correction."
The Thread shows the Correction as the old value crossed out, an arrow and the new value. The Metric Owner hears about it. Until they decide, others see "Waiting for the metric owner … to accept."
The Metric Owner sees two buttons:
Accept: the new value takes the old one's place, and the Correction is marked Corrected. Ziffr keeps the…

sections.heading: Answering by email or Slack
sections.text:
Each new Action, reply, proposed Correction and closed Task reaches the person as a Delivery: by email, on Slack, by Telegram or through another Connector, as they chose under Your Deliveries (see Your settings).
People answer by replying to that email, Slack or Telegram message. In Telegram, they reply to the message itself (swipe it to the left, or press and hold it and choose Reply); a message that replies to nothing gets a hint instead, so no answer lands on the wrong question. Their answer goes into the Thread, as if they had written it in Ziffr. A line starting with "Correction:" and a…

sections.heading: The Changes page
sections.text: Open Workspace → Changes. The page lists every change to what people build, and every number that was replaced, newest first. Nothing on it can be edited. Everyone in the Workspace can open it, and each person sees only what they may see. A Guest sees changes to what is shared with them and to the Workflows of those Metrics, not to templates or Themes.

sections.heading: What it lists
sections.text:
Changes to things people build: someone created, edited or restored a Widget, dashboard, deck, Metric description, team Widget Template or Dashboard Template, Theme, Workflow or the words of a Snapshot, or gave a Version a name. Each line names the person and the thing, shows the Version number (such as "v3") and links to the thing where it has a page. Edits by one person within ten minutes count as one Version.
Replaced values: "A value" lines say that a value of a Metric for a period was replaced or removed, with the old value. The old value is kept as a Superseded Value. A value that…

sections.heading: Filtering by person
sections.text: The row of names at the top filters the list. It names the people behind the changes you see, not everyone in the Workspace. Everyone shows all entries; a first name shows only that person's changes. Replaced values are not tied to a person, so they show only under Everyone.

sections.heading: Changes, Versions and the Audit Log
sections.text: Changes shows what changed. To see or restore an earlier state, open Versions on the thing itself. Who changed who may see or do what (roles, Shares, Locks, Approvals and the like) is kept in the Audit Log, which only Owners and Admins read (see Workspace settings).

sections.heading: Workspace settings
sections.text:
A Workspace is your team's own space in Ziffr. This chapter goes through its pages one by one: how a Workspace starts, how people join it, and every page behind the Workspace row of the sidebar.
Everyone in the Workspace opens these pages, but what each person may change depends on their Workspace Role:
A Workspace can have several Owners, and it always keeps at least one.

sections.heading: The Workspace menu
sections.text:
Choose Workspace in the sidebar to open its pages. They are:
A Guest sees only what is shared with them, and never who else is in the Workspace: other people's names, emails and Slack handles do not appear anywhere. Whoever owns, edits, approves or comments on what is shared with them reads as "Someone", Who can see this shows them only their own line ("Viewer", or "Viewer through" a Group they are in), and search finds only themselves. A Version history of a Theme is not open to them. Their Connectors page shows their own Delivery Preferences, their Workflows are those of the Metrics shared…

sections.heading: In the sidebar
sections.text: In the sidebar (see Signing in and your own settings) the Workspace row opens four places: Members and Groups, Workflows, Connectors (with tabs for Channels, Sources, Outbox and Who gets what) and Settings. Guests have no Workspace row. Settings is one page with its own list, shown beside whichever of its pages is open, in three groups: Workspace (General, Size and Retention for Owners and Admins, Themes, Packs), Programs (Access Keys, and Feeds and Webhooks for Owners and Admins) and Records (Changes, and Usage and Audit log for Owners and Admins). Your own pages are not in that list: they…

sections.heading: Starting a Workspace
sections.text:
After you sign in for the first time and belong to no Workspace yet, Ziffr opens Start a workspace, in the same plain column as the sign-in page: the Ziffr mark and a card with the form. Start your trial, an Invitation's page and the Trial guide share that look.
Type the Name of the workspace, such as your name, your team or your company, and choose Create workspace. You become its Owner, and Ziffr opens it.
If a colleague already uses Ziffr, it is better to ask them to invite you, so you join their Workspace instead of starting a second one.
You can start another Workspace at any time from…

sections.heading: From a Workspace Export
sections.text:
On a Ziffr that you or your company run (not on hosted Ziffr, where a new Workspace is a trial), Start a workspace also says "Coming from another Ziffr?" with a link, Start from a Workspace Export. Choose the file the Owner of the other Workspace downloaded and select Import. The file becomes a new Workspace and you are its Owner; nothing is merged into a Workspace you already have.
Ziffr first checks the whole file and writes nothing. If anything is wrong, such as a line that is not allowed, a number that is too large, a name the file never listed, a time zone this Ziffr does not know, or…

sections.heading: On a Ziffr that offers trials
sections.text: Hosted Ziffr offers Trial Workspaces instead; a Ziffr that somebody else runs has none, and every Workspace made there is an ordinary one. What the page then says works in a trial, email first, follows what this Ziffr is set up with, also on its Installation settings page. The sign-in page then says, in one line under its heading, that a new address gets an account from the same link; the demo, where it is offered, is a small Try the demo link below the form. Where the Ziffr has set it up, a short check against bots by Cloudflare sits above Send me a sign-in link; the button works once it has…

sections.heading: Asking to join
sections.text:
If your colleagues' Workspace has Domain Joining switched on, and you signed in with a proven address at the same company domain, the page shows Your colleagues already use Ziffr above the form. It lists each such Workspace with an Ask to join button.
After you ask, the line says "Asked; an owner or admin decides." An Owner or Admin sees your name and address on Members and Groups and lets you in or declines. If they let you in, you join as a Member.
Addresses at public mail providers, such as Gmail or Outlook, never count as a company domain.

sections.heading: Accepting an Invitation
sections.text:
An Invitation reaches you as an email or as a link someone sends you. Opening it asks you to sign in first, then shows Join followed by the Workspace's name and the role you are invited with, such as "You are invited as Member".
Choose Join. You become part of the Workspace with that role, and Ziffr opens it.
An Invitation sent to an email address works only for that address. If you are signed in with another one, the page says so: sign out and sign in with the invited address.
When the Workspace is a trial, the page says so under its title: who invited you, the day the trial ends and what…

sections.heading: General
sections.text: Workspace → General holds the Workspace's name, its time, its fiscal year, its Number Style, its Answer Languages, its limits and its Workspace Profile. Owners and Admins change them. Everyone else sees them, with the note "Only Owners and Admins change these."

sections.heading: Size and usage
sections.text:
Owners and Admins see Size and usage under the name: how many Metrics the Workspace holds, Archived Metrics not counted. When the Workspace has a Workspace Limit, it also shows the Size, such as "Small", and the count of the limit, such as "38 of 50 Metrics"; and a coming change, such as "Changes to Team on 1 December 2026", when one is set. Without a limit, as on most self-hosted Ziffrs, it shows only the count.
Over its limit, the section says since when and until when new Metrics can still be made (14 days, with room for 10 % more), or that they wait now. Everything else keeps working and…

sections.heading: Name
sections.text: The Workspace name is what everyone sees in the Workspace switcher and in Invitations. Type a new one (up to 80 characters) and choose Save.

sections.heading: Quiet hours
sections.text: On the same page as the Workspace's time, Owners and Admins can set the default Quiet hours for everyone who has set none of their own: the hours (such as 19:00 until 07:00) and the whole days (such as Saturday and Sunday) when Ziffr sends no request for numbers, reminder, Alert or Heads-up message. They wait and go out when the quiet hours end. The default is read in the Workspace's time zone; people can set their own, in their own time zone, under Your Deliveries. Remove takes the default away. It is recorded in the Audit Log.

sections.heading: Workspace time
sections.text:
Ziffr counts days, working days and Due Dates in the Workspace's own time. An assistant connected to Ziffr can read the time zone, the hour Ziffr asks at and the first day of the week, so that "ask me at 1 pm" means 13:00 here.
Choose Save after changing any of them. Members and Guests see a single line, such as "Europe/Berlin, Workflows run at 07:00, weeks start on Monday".

sections.heading: Fiscal year
sections.text:
Year starts in sets the month the Workspace's Fiscal Year begins. It decides where quarters, half-years and years start everywhere in Ziffr: for quarterly and yearly Metrics, their Prompts and Due Dates, in Comparisons such as QoQ and HoH, in a widget's Show by, and in Snapshots of a quarter, half-year or year. Programs read it through the API (GET /api/v1/workspace). It is January unless an Owner or Admin picks another month.
With January, quarters and years have their calendar names: "Q3 2026", "H2 2026", "2026". With any other month, a year is named by both calendar years it spans, so it…

sections.heading: Number style
sections.text: Numbers look like sets the Workspace's Number Style. It is one of four: 1,234.5, 1.234,5, 1 234,5 and 1'234.5. Each choice shows a percentage too, such as "1.234,5 (12,5 %)". The style says which mark groups the digits and which mark is the decimal. Ziffr writes every value in it: on every page, in charts, in replies by Slack, Telegram and email, and in decks. A negative number is written with the minus sign "−", values and changes alike, such as "−1.200 €" or "−3,5 %". Files and programs get a plain "-": the CSV download, the API and the MCP Server. Ziffr reads either sign when you type or…

sections.heading: Answer languages
sections.text:
People often answer a Prompt in a sentence, such as "letzte Woche 2" or "la semaine dernière 2". Answer languages says which languages' words Ziffr understands there. Ziffr reads those words as the period, never as the value (see How Ziffr reads a number you send). Tick the languages your people answer in: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Dutch. Ziffr tries only the ticked ones, so a word that means one thing in one language and another elsewhere never gets in the way.
Until an Owner or Admin picks languages, the Workspace reads English plus the languages of the country in its…

sections.heading: Attainment
sections.text:
Attainment is computed sets how the percentage of target is worked out for every Metric that has no method of its own. By ratio divides the value by the target, or the target by the value when lower is better. By distance counts the distance to the target in steps of the target's size. They agree for "higher is better" with a target above 0, and differ for "lower is better" and around 0: 5 against a target of at most 10 is 200 % by ratio and 150 % by distance. Metrics explains both.
Every Workspace computes by ratio until an Owner or Admin changes it, as Ziffr did up to version 0.9.0. A…

sections.heading: Retention
sections.text:
Retention sets the default for new Metrics: keep values for 2, 3, 5, 7 or 10 years (or a number of months, at least 13), then condense them into longer periods or delete them. Without one, every value is kept for ever. Only Owners set it, since it decides what every Metric made afterwards starts with and deleting cannot be undone; Admins see it, Members and Guests do not see the section. The demo has none.
The default is copied into a new Metric when it is made, with no link back: changing it later changes no Metric that exists. A Metric it does not fit (a rate cannot be condensed) gets none,…

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text:
For Owners and Admins, a section Limits lists five values the Workspace may set for itself, each within the range its Installation allows. Under each field it says what is In effect and the range Allowed; leave the field empty to follow the Installation, and press Save to set or clear it.
Alerts per person (1 up to the Installation's ceiling; normal 20): the most Alerts one person may hold in this Workspace.
Alert messages per person per day (1 up to the Installation's ceiling; normal 20): after it, Alerts still fire into the list and only the messages wait for tomorrow. Each person may lower…

sections.heading: Workspace Profile
sections.text:
The Workspace Profile says what kind of business this is, so Ziffr can suggest the Metrics such teams track. Each part is picked from a list; Not set leaves it open.
Choose Save when you are done. Teams within your company, such as Sales or Finance, are not part of the profile: make them Groups on Members and Groups.

sections.heading: Encryption
sections.text: Owners see one line at the end of the page: Encrypted with a key of its own. Deleting this Workspace destroys it. The Workspace's words and numbers (Thread replies, questions and tasks, Contacts' details, Metric names, values, notes on a period, the Outbox, the Audit Log and the Slack connection's token) are encrypted with that key as they are written, and what was written before is encrypted as Ziffr gets to it, so a copy of the database alone does not show what is already encrypted. Ziffr itself still reads them to do its work: this is not end-to-end encryption. When a Workspace is deleted…

sections.heading: Workspace Export
sections.text:
Only the Workspace's Owner sees Workspace Export under Settings, in the Workspace group. It downloads what you may see in the Workspace as one file, to keep or for another Ziffr to read as a new Workspace. The page first says what the file will hold (how many Metrics, dashboards, decks, Workflows, Themes, Groups, Shares and people to invite) and what stays out, with the reason for each. With every Metric come its values, Target Series and Projections.
The file holds every value in the clear, so keep it as private as the Workspace. Ziffr makes it while you download it and keeps no copy; the…

sections.heading: In the demo
sections.text:
The demo's sidebar has the same user menu at the bottom as any Workspace: My schedule, Profile, Deliveries and Alerts open from it, so a visitor does not have to find them in the side list. Under Dashboards the demo's sidebar shows a few pinned dashboards (pinning is off there, so they stay as they are). A change the demo refuses says "The demo can't be changed." with Try it with a trial of your own beside it.
In the demo nobody changes these settings: the page shows them without the controls and says "The demo can't be changed." The demo has no Workspace time: its date is the pretend date on…

sections.heading: Members and Groups
sections.text: Workspace → Members and Groups shows everyone in the Workspace, their roles, their Groups, their Away dates and the Contacts. Owners, Admins and Members see it; only Owners and Admins see the buttons that change people and Groups. A Guest sees only what is shared with them, so the page shows them none of this.

sections.heading: Members and their roles
sections.text:
The list shows each person with their role. Owners and Admins see a menu next to each person instead:
Pick another role and it changes at once. Only an Owner can make someone an Owner or change an Owner's role. The last Owner cannot step down: make someone else Owner first.

sections.heading: Removing someone and handing over
sections.text:
A person who owns Metrics cannot be changed to Guest: hand the Metrics over first (see Handing a Metric over in the Metrics chapter), or remove them and pick who takes over.
Choose Remove… next to a person. Ziffr asks who takes over their Metrics and everything else, and offers an Owner first: keep that choice or pick another person (not a Guest), then choose Remove, or Cancel to stop.
When you remove someone:
Everything they own, such as their Metrics, dashboards, decks, Workflows, Themes and saved templates, goes to the person who takes over. Nothing others built on is deleted, and the…

sections.heading: Inviting people
sections.text:
Owners and Admins see the invitation form below the list.
After either, the page shows the link so you can send it yourself, for example in a chat. The message says what really happened: "Invitation emailed to …" when the email went out, "Invitation made: copy the link and send it yourself, email is not set up" when this Ziffr sends no email, and a note that the email could not be sent when mail is set up but the send failed.
An email Invitation works for 14 days, once, and only for that address.
A link works for 7 days, for anyone who has it, until it ends or you revoke it.
Below the form,…

sections.heading: Requests to join
sections.text: When someone asks to join through Domain Joining, their name and address appear with "asks to join". Choose Let in to make them a Member, or Decline.

sections.heading: Domain Joining
sections.text:
Owners see a checkbox such as "Let people with an address at example.com ask to join". It uses the domain of the address you signed in with, so your address must be proven. Once it is on, the line reads "People with an address at example.com may ask to join", and anyone signing in with an address at that domain sees your Workspace on their welcome page. Nobody gets in by themselves: an Owner or Admin lets each one in.
Domain Joining is off by default and does not work for public mail providers.

sections.heading: Groups and Away dates
sections.text:
The table below the members has one row per person and these columns:
Person: their name and job.
Away: the dates they are not available, from and to. While someone is Away, Prompts meant for them go to their Stand-in. Each person sets their own dates here or under Your Deliveries. Owners and Admins can set them for anyone. Clear removes them.
One column per Group: a tick means the person is in that Group.
A Group is a named set of people, such as Management or Sales. You share things with a Group, or limit a question's Thread to one, and whoever joins the Group later gets the same. Owners…

sections.heading: Contacts
sections.text:
A Contact is someone without a login, such as a field worker or an outside bookkeeper. They send in values by Slack, by email or with their personal form link, and the values are recorded under their name. They see nothing in Ziffr.
Owners and Admins add a Contact with Name and at least one of Email, Slack handle (such as @cleo) or Phone, then Add contact. The address or handle must not belong to anyone else in the Workspace. Owners and Admins also see each Contact's details, and the bin icon removes a Contact. A Workspace keeps 1,000 Contacts unless the person who runs this Ziffr has set…

sections.heading: Connectors
sections.text: Workspace → Connectors shows how Ziffr reaches people and how their answers come back. Everyone sees it. See Connecting Ziffr for the bigger picture. It has five tabs, each its own page: Channels (below, from Slack to Connected systems), Sources, Send values, Outbox and Who gets what. The old address /sources leads to the Sources tab. Claude and other AI assistants are not set up here but under Connected assistants in your own menu; Channels says so in one line.

sections.heading: Send values
sections.text: The Send values tab is where everyone finds a working way to put values on their Metrics from a program or another system. Pick one of your Metrics that takes values from the API (its Values arrive by includes API and Feeds), and a kind of key: a Feed Key for a system (Owners and Admins; up to 500 values in one call) or an Access Key for you (one value at a time, as you). The page shows the call for this Ziffr's own address in curl, JavaScript, Python and n8n or Zapier, each with a Copy button. The key is a placeholder: the page holds no key and sends nothing (make a key under Settings →…

sections.heading: Slack
sections.text:
The Slack box appears when this Ziffr is set up for Slack (never in the demo).
Once Slack is connected, the box says how Slack knows you: by your email address, or because you linked your account. If your Slack address differs from the one you sign in with, link your account.
A Slack workspace can be connected to one Ziffr Workspace only.

sections.heading: Telegram
sections.text:
The Telegram box appears when this Ziffr has a Telegram bot (never in the demo). Whoever runs this Ziffr sets the bot up, in the server's settings or on the Installation settings page; if Telegram does not accept its token, the box says so and points them there. It names the bot, such as @acmeziffrbot, and says whether Telegram is on in this Workspace. It is off until an Owner or Admin turns it on.
A bot cannot find anyone by email or phone number, so everyone connects their own Telegram, once per Workspace. Contacts without a login connect it on their personal form. To stop everything from…

sections.heading: Claude and other AI assistants
sections.text: How to connect an AI assistant through the MCP Server is on Connected assistants in your own menu (see Connecting an assistant), filled in with this Ziffr's address; Channels has one line that links there. It is not shown in the demo, which has no Access Keys. Assistants that use an Access Key need one made first (see Access Keys).

sections.heading: Connected systems
sections.text:
One card per Connector, each with what it can do (receives values, sends reminders, sends questions and tasks, brings replies back, keeps task status in step) and its state. A badge says Real (it really goes out), Simulated (Ziffr only keeps it in the Outbox) or Off, followed by why and, in a Trial Workspace, the limit that applies, such as "To you only, at most 50 messages a day":
If you stopped Prompts and reminders by email, a note at the top of Channels offers Get them by email again. On a card whose Connector is only simulated, an Installation Admin gets Set it up on Installation…

sections.heading: Who gets what, where
sections.text:
The Who gets what tab: a table of Delivery Preferences: one row per person and one column each for Questions, Tasks, Prompts and reminders and Replies and updates.
The first row, Team default, covers everyone who leaves a column open. Only Owners and Admins change it. Without a team default, Ziffr uses email.
Your own row is marked "you". Change it here or under Your Deliveries. Everyone else's row is greyed out.
Under Prompts and reminders a person can pick up to three ways, in order: the first select is the first way, the others are Also by. A Prompt goes by every way in the list at once…

sections.heading: Outbox
sections.text:
The Outbox tab lists every Delivery you may see, newest first, drawn the way it looks on the other side. Each one shows the Connector, who it went to, when, whether it was answered or closed, and Open thread for a question or task.
A Delivery that never left Ziffr is marked Simulated, not sent, or with the reason it was kept back, such as "Kept in the Outbox: a trial never sends to a Contact". For email, Slack and Telegram, a small label says whether it really went out: Waiting to send, Sending, Emailed, Sent on Slack, Sent on Telegram or Not sent with the reason, such as "Not connected to…

sections.heading: In the demo
sections.text: The two Run now buttons sit in a dashed Demo controls box; using them says "The demo can't be changed." Under each Delivery you can play the recipient: Answer as the person, then Send in the Connector, or Close ticket as the person for a ticket. Ziffr then says what would happen, such as that the answer would land in the thread or that the value would be recorded, and saves nothing. Try sending a value on the Email and Slack cards leads to the Sources tab.

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text: Workspace → Connectors → Sources shows where values come from. Everyone sees it. It names only the Metrics you can see: a message or form link about a Metric you cannot see shows no name.

sections.heading: From the web form
sections.text: When you have sent values on the web form, From the web form lists the latest 20, newest first: when, the Metric, what was sent, and what happened, in the same words the form or the paste answered. A value from a paste is marked "pasted", or "pasted as history" when it was recorded as history. You see only your own, except in the demo.

sections.heading: Form links
sections.text: Everyone who sends in a Metric has a personal form link for it. The link itself is the permission, so nobody needs to sign in. You see your own links here, one per Metric that takes the web form, and opening one shows the form. If you have none, the page says a Metric gets them when its owner picks the web form as a Source and names who submits.

sections.heading: The simulator (demo only)
sections.text:
In the demo, a Demo controls box shows two pretend inboxes, one for Slack and one for email, both marked "simulated". They go through the same checks as real ones, but save nothing: each message you send shows what would happen, and stays on the page, marked "not saved", until you leave it.
Pick who sends the message, including an unknown sender, type a message such as "closed 2 deals", and send it.
Under a Prompt from Ziffr, choose Reply to answer it as its recipient.
Each message shows what happened, or for one you sent, what would happen ("Would be: Recorded"), such as Recorded,…

sections.heading: Packs
sections.text: Packs, ready-made Metric Catalog entries, templates, designs and Themes, have a chapter of their own: Packs. Open them with Workspace → Packs.

sections.heading: Tags
sections.text:
Workspace → Tags lists the Workspace's Tags, the free words people put on Metrics, each with how many Metrics carry it; the count links to the Metrics list filtered by that Tag. You see a Tag, and count its Metrics, only through Metrics you may see: a Tag that only Metrics out of your sight carry is not listed to you. Members see the list and change nothing. Guests have no Tags page.
Owners and Admins change the words for the whole Workspace:
Rename changes a Tag's spelling on every Metric. If another Tag you can see already has the name, Ziffr asks you to merge the two instead.
Merge into……

sections.heading: Access Keys
sections.text:
Workspace → Access Keys is where you make an Access Key: a secret that lets a program or an AI assistant work in this Workspace on your behalf. A key sees no more than you do, and it stops working when it ends, when it is revoked, or when you leave the Workspace.
An assistant someone connected by Ziffr's address, such as Claude.ai, is listed here too, marked Connected assistant and named as it named itself (see Connected assistants). Revoking it disconnects it. Owners and Admins see every connection with its recent calls, and Owners can end anyone's.
In a Trial Workspace, at most two Access…

sections.heading: Making a key
sections.text: The last three change who sees what, so only a key you make here can hold them: a connected assistant is never offered them. The secret is shown once: copy it now, it is not shown again. Give it only to the program that needs it.

sections.heading: The list of keys
sections.text:
Each key shows its name, what it may do, the day it ends (or "revoked") and, for someone else's key, who made it.
Recent calls opens the key's Access Log: when the program called, what it asked for, and the result. A failed call shows in red.
The bin icon revokes the key at once.
The demo has no Access Keys, because a key there would act as a made-up person for anyone.

sections.heading: Calendar Links
sections.text: Owners and Admins also see, below the keys, who has a Calendar Link: a secret address that shows a person's schedule in their calendar app (see My schedule and your calendar). Each line shows the person's name, when they made it, and when a calendar last fetched it. The address itself is never shown. The bin icon revokes the link at once, and it then answers "not found". Its person can make a new one. A Calendar Link also ends when its person leaves the Workspace.

sections.heading: Feeds
sections.text:
Workspace → Feeds is for Owners and Admins only. Others see a note to ask an Owner or Admin. The demo has no Feeds.
A Feed brings in values from another system, such as a CRM or a data warehouse. It runs outside Ziffr, with a Feed Key that can only record values for the Metrics that take the Feed as a Submitter, never read them. It belongs to the Workspace and keeps working when the person who set it up leaves. See Connecting Ziffr for how Feeds work.

sections.heading: Making a Feed
sections.text: Under New Feed, type a name, ideally the system it brings values from, such as "HubSpot", and choose Create Feed. Then choose the Feed as a Submitter on each Metric's Description tab.

sections.heading: Feed Keys
sections.text:
Each Feed lists its keys with name, the start of the key, and the day it ends or "revoked". Recent calls opens its Access Log; the bin icon revokes it.
To make a key, type a Key name (such as "Nightly run"; if you leave it empty, Ziffr names it after the Feed), pick Until (at most a year ahead) and choose Create Feed Key. The secret is shown once. Copy it and give it to whoever runs the Feed.
Only Owners and Admins see Feed Keys and their Access Logs.
To fill Metrics from a sheet or another system without writing a Feed, use Fill from n8n under a Metric's Who submits (see The Metrics screens)…

sections.heading: Webhooks
sections.text:
Workspace → Webhooks is for Owners and Admins only. Others see a note to ask an Owner or Admin. The demo has no Webhooks. A trial may add Webhooks within smaller limits, which are Trial Limits (by default 2 Webhooks and 200 sends a day; the Try it guide shows the number in force, and offers none where trials may have no Webhooks), and only to public addresses (the private hosts an operator allows for other Workspaces never apply to a trial). Whoever runs this Ziffr can switch Webhooks off for trials (Installation settings, Trials); then a trial cannot add one and those it has send nothing.
In…

sections.heading: Adding a Webhook
sections.text:
Type a name, ideally the system it feeds, such as "Microsoft To Do", and the address, which must start with https:// and may not hold a user name, a password or a #. Tick the events it gets, then choose Add Webhook. Ziffr refuses an address inside its own network.
The secret appears once, in a box above the list. Copy it before you choose I have copied it: Ziffr cannot show it again. The receiver uses it to check each message's signature.

sections.heading: Alerts to a Webhook
sections.text: The event A Tell step fires (alert.fired) is sent only when a Workflow's Tell step names the Webhook (see Workflows), once per crossing. The message holds the Metric, its period, the value and target as the Alert message writes them, the condition that became true and a link, and nothing else. It goes out only for a Metric shared with Everyone, and Ziffr checks that again at the moment of sending, so a Metric made private meanwhile, a value sent back for Approval or a Workflow whose owner is no longer an Owner or Admin sends nothing. A person's own Alerts never reach a Workspace Webhook; they…

sections.heading: The log
sections.text:
Under each Webhook, Log lists its sends of the last 14 days: when, the event, what it is about (a task's reference such as ZIF-12, or a Metric's number), the state (waiting, will try again, delivered, failed, not sent), the answer's status and how many tries it took. It holds no message text and no answer. A failed send has Send again.
Every change to a Webhook is in the Audit log, and the other Owners get an email.

sections.heading: Personal Webhooks
sections.text:
Below the Workspace's own Webhooks, Workspace → Webhooks has a second list, Personal Webhooks, and the switch People may add their own Webhooks. A Personal Webhook is an address that one person adds for themselves under You → Your Webhooks (see Signing in and your own settings). It hears only what that person may see at the moment it is sent, and it acts as them.
The switch is off until an Owner or Admin switches it on, for every Workspace. Switching it off pauses every Personal Webhook: nothing is sent to them, what happens in the meantime is not sent later, and each person's page says why.…

sections.heading: Usage
sections.text:
Workspace → Usage is for Owners and Admins; Members and Guests do not see it, and the demo has none, because it counts nothing. It shows what could be tidied up, as lists with the reason beside each name:
Dashboards, decks and Metrics not opened for 90 days. A Metric counts as opened when its own page was opened or when it is on a dashboard or deck that was. A Metric that only a program reads, such as an assistant, is listed apart as Only read by a program and never suggested for archiving. Anything made less than 90 days ago is not listed.
Metrics without values: none ever, or none for 90…

sections.heading: Your Usage as Metrics
sections.text: If you want these figures as Metrics of their own, with a dashboard, Targets and Alerts, install the Workspace usage Pack (Workspace → Packs → Choose a Pack file…, packs/workspace-usage.pack.json) and use Set up from this Pack. A program then sends the figures: make an Access Key with Read usage figures and a Feed with a Feed Key, and run the Usage Feed with --workspace (see the Usage guide). They are ordinary Metrics: the Pack has 18 of them, they count towards the Workspace Limit, and everyone who sees them sees the numbers, so while fewer than three people are in the Workspace the values,…

sections.heading: The monthly email
sections.text: Owners (not Admins) get one plain-text email a month about the same lists, in the first days of the month, only when something is unused. It says how many dashboards, decks and Metrics were not opened for 90 days, how many Metrics have no values and how many Submitters have sent none, names at most five of each ("and 3 more") and links to this page. It holds no values, no counts per item and no answers, and it names only what that Owner sees on the page. It is never sent for the demo, for a trial, for a workspace still within its first 90 days of counting, or when nothing is unused, and never…

sections.heading: Audit log
sections.text:
Workspace → Audit log is for Owners and Admins only. It is the Audit Log: who changed who may see or do what, and the decisions taken on numbers. Nothing in it can be changed or removed, and events are kept for two years, or for the days the Installation Admin has set (the page says how long). Times are shown in the Workspace's time zone.
On a phone the filter (Person, What happened, From, To, Show) stacks one field under the other, and the row of Settings pages above it scrolls sideways and fades out at its right edge to say so.

sections.heading: What is recorded
sections.text: Role changes and removals, Invitations, requests to join, Domain Joining, Contacts, Shares, Groups, View Links, Access Keys, Feeds and Feed Keys, Webhooks (added, changed, given a new secret, switched on or off, deleted), new dashboards, new, deleted, archived and brought back Metrics, a Metric's Workflow, a Metric's Retention (set or cancelled) and the Workspace's default Retention, Locks, Workflow runs, Approvals (and values counted without one because nobody else could approve them), Self-checks, Corrections, each Filled-in Value (who filled in a value, for whom, for which period and as…

sections.heading: Filters
sections.text: Click a person's name in the list to see only their events. Click what an event was about to see only events about that one thing; Show all goes back. A filtered view is a link you can keep. Older events shows the next page.

sections.heading: Download CSV
sections.text: Download CSV saves the events of the current filter as a spreadsheet file, at most 50,000 at a time; pick dates for more. Each download is itself recorded in the Audit Log, and a Workspace can download it at most ten times an hour.

chapters.title: Signing in and your own settings

sections.heading: Signing in and your own settings
sections.text: This chapter covers what is yours rather than the team's: signing in, the demo, the sidebar, and your own pages: My schedule, Your profile, Appearance, Your Deliveries and Your Alerts. Everyone has them, whatever their role. The team's pages are in Workspace settings.

sections.heading: Signing in
sections.text:
The page Sign in to Ziffr opens whenever you are not signed in. It is one plain column: the Ziffr mark, a card with the form, and below it Try the demo where your Ziffr offers the demo. It looks the same on a phone, and follows your Appearance, dark included.
Where the Ziffr has set it up, a short check against bots by Cloudflare sits above the button; the email link and any other way to sign in work once it has passed. If the check fails or Cloudflare cannot be reached, no link is sent, and a new check appears for the next try. If a sign-in link did not work or was used already, the page…

sections.heading: Imprint, Privacy notice and Terms
sections.text: On hosted Ziffr (the Ziffr you reach at ziffr.net) three links sit at the foot of every page: Imprint, Privacy notice and Terms. They are on the sign-in page, in the app, in the demo and on View Link pages, and each opens Ziffr's own page in a new tab. Where an account can be created, the sign-in page also says "By signing up you agree to the Terms and the Privacy notice." under the button. A Ziffr that someone runs themselves shows none of this and has no setting for it.

sections.heading: The demo
sections.text: Demo Mode is a visit to a made-up online shop with its own made-up people. Every visitor shares it, and nothing done there is saved or reaches a real Workspace. It is the place to look around before you start; see also Getting started.

sections.heading: Opening the demo
sections.text:
Choose Try the demo on the sign-in page. If you are already signed in, Ziffr first asks Open the demo?: nothing you do there is saved, so your own numbers belong in your own Workspace. Choose Open the demo, or Stay in my workspace.
While you are in the demo, the footer of the sidebar shows your menu with Viewing as, your own pages and Leave the demo.

sections.heading: Demo controls
sections.text: Some pages have a dashed box marked Demo controls. Its buttons show what would happen by itself in a real Workspace, such as answering as the recipient of a message or starting the morning's Prompts by hand. You never see them outside the demo.

sections.heading: Nothing is saved
sections.text:
You can open every page, switch between the people and try every button and form, but the demo can't be changed: where something would be saved, Ziffr says "The demo can't be changed." Where this Ziffr offers trials, it adds a link, "Try it with a trial of your own." A form with no place of its own for the answer shows it on a screen headed Nothing was saved; Back returns to the form.
The simulators on Connectors → Sources and in the Outbox answer with what would happen, such as "Would be: Recorded", and keep nothing. What you tried in the Sources simulator stays on the page until you leave…

sections.heading: The guided tour
sections.text:
In the demo, the Guided tour sits at the bottom right. Choose it to open the steps, and click a step to go to its page:
The tour reads first, because the demo can't be changed:
1. Look at a dashboard and click a number to see its history.
2. See what others see: switch Viewing as to Anna and to the Guest.
3. Analyze: run a Recipe and look at what it finds.
4. Open a deck and click through its slides.
5. Capture a value by answering a Slack Prompt, and send a second one to see the Submission Rule.
6. Define a metric from the catalog; the demo won't save it, which is what a trial is for.
A…

sections.heading: The sidebar
sections.text: The sidebar is on every page once you are in a Workspace. At its top is the Workspace switcher, then a Search field (Ctrl+K), Schedule with its count (values due, and answered Actions waiting for you to close), Dashboards (with the dashboards you pinned under it, or in the demo a few already pinned, see Pinning a dashboard), Metrics, Decks, Analyze and one Workspace row that opens Members and Groups, Workflows, Connectors and Settings (closed unless you are on one of them; Guests do not see it). Help (it opens the user guide beside the page, see Help beside the page) and your own menu (Your…

sections.heading: Help beside the page
sections.text: The ? button at the right of the bar above every page (Help for this screen) opens a panel on the right with the part of this user guide that describes the screen you are on: its sections, each with Read this section. Help in the sidebar (on a phone, in More) opens the same panel at the list of chapters instead, the one for this screen first and marked "this screen"; in the panel, All chapters and About this screen switch between the two. Above them is a search box, Search the user guide, that looks through every chapter and lists what it finds with the chapter and section it is from. The…

sections.heading: Search
sections.text:
Press ⌘K (on Windows and Linux Ctrl+K), or choose the magnifying glass, and type. Ziffr finds the Metrics, dashboards, decks and Workflows whose names fit what you typed, ignoring capitals and accents, and only those you may see in the Workspace you are in. A Metric that is archived is marked Archived, and listed after the ones in use. Results are grouped: Commands, Pages, Metrics, Tags, Dashboards, Decks, Workflows, People and Groups.
