Tags. Type a word that is one of your Metrics' Tags, such as "finance", and Search offers Tag: finance (7 Metrics), which opens the Metrics list filtered by…

sections.heading: On a phone
sections.text:
On a phone the demo's note is one line, the guided tour starts as a small round button, and everything you press is at least 44 px high. The row of Settings pages scrolls sideways and fades out at the edge to say so.
Ziffr works best on a phone once you install it: it then opens from the home screen like an app, with the same layout. See Put Ziffr on your phone or desktop.

sections.heading: The Schedule and your calendar
sections.text: Open the Schedule row of the sidebar (with the number of values due). Its address is /schedule; the old /settings/schedule still lands on it, and the old Actions page, /actions, lands on its Asked by me view. The Schedule has three views, switched at the top: To do (the default, described here), Asked by me and Timeline (see Actions and Changes). To do lists what you have to do in the current Workspace, and only that. All, Values, Approvals, Tasks and Questions above it narrow the list to one kind; Waiting for your confirmation lists any Share Proposals an assistant prepared (see Actions and…

sections.heading: List, Week and Month
sections.text:
Above the schedule a switch chooses how it is shown: List (the lines above), Week or Month. Ziffr remembers your choice in this browser. The week and the month show the same duties on their days, nothing more; use the arrows to move to other weeks and months, up to about three months ahead, and Today to come back.
Week has a column for each day, from the Workspace's first day of the week (Monday, unless an Owner or Admin chose Sunday in Workspace → General), with today marked. Each duty is a small card in its kind's colour, with its words as in the list; click it to open what the list line…

sections.heading: In your calendar
sections.text:
A Calendar Link puts your schedule in your calendar app, next to your meetings: each date as an all-day entry, such as "Revenue for October 2026 due" or "Approve: Cost for October 2026", from 30 days back to 90 days ahead. Something late stays on its own date, with "(overdue)" in its title. Entries without a date are left out. Each entry links to where you do it in Ziffr, and the link asks you to sign in. Nothing you do in the calendar changes anything in Ziffr.
To subscribe, paste the address:
Apple Calendar: File → New Calendar Subscription. Choose to refresh every hour.
Google Calendar:…

sections.heading: Your profile
sections.text:
Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar. Your profile is how others see you in every Workspace you belong to: a change shows in all of them.
In the demo, the made-up people keep their names and colours, the address is made up, and the last button is Leave the demo instead of Sign out.

sections.heading: Your limits
sections.text:
Under your profile, Your limits lets you choose how much of this Workspace you want, in this Workspace only. Each field shows what is In effect and the range Allowed; leave it empty to follow the Workspace, and press Save to set or clear it. You can only go lower than what the Workspace allows.
Alert messages per person per day: the most Alert messages you are sent in a day (1 up to what the Workspace allows). After it your Alerts still fire into the list.
How far back the overdue list reaches (7 to 90 days; normal 90): overdue entries older than this are left off your Schedule.
Calendar…

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text:
Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar. It decides how Ziffr's own screens look to you, including the sign-in page. Pick one of four, each shown as a small preview; the page changes at once.
The choice is saved to you, so every device and every Workspace you use looks the same. A browser that is not signed in, such as the sign-in page, uses the choice last made in it, and System before any. In the demo nothing is saved, so the choice stays in this browser.
Dashboards and Decks follow your Appearance too: when it is dark, a Theme shows its dark variant, unless the Theme is set…

sections.heading: Your Deliveries
sections.text: Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar, or from Deliveries in the settings area. A Delivery is one message Ziffr sends you through a Connector. This page sets where those messages go in the current Workspace, and who is asked while you are away. You can only change your own.

sections.heading: Where you get what
sections.text:
Your Delivery Preference for each kind of message:
For each, pick Email, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp or Ticket system, or leave it at Team default (which shows what the team default is). Owners and Admins set the team default on the Connectors page. A change is saved at once.
Prompts and reminders can go by up to three ways at once, for example Slack, Telegram and email. Pick the first way, then Also by a second and a third. The order matters: a Prompt goes by every way in your list at the same time, and the first answer on any of them counts. The other messages are updated where the app allows…

sections.heading: Requests for numbers by email
sections.text:
The box Send me Prompts and reminders by email in this workspace is ticked while you get them. Untick it to stop them. Questions, tasks and replies keep coming, and the owners of the Metrics you send in are told once that you stopped. Tick it again to get them back. The same happens when you use the unsubscribe link in one of these emails.
If your Ziffr sends no email, the box cannot be ticked and the page says so.

sections.heading: Unused Metrics by email
sections.text: Owners also see Email me when Metrics, dashboards or decks go unused. It is ticked at first. It is the monthly usage email described under Usage in Workspace settings, and it is one setting for all the workspaces you own, not one per workspace. Untick it to stop the email, tick it again to get it back. The unsubscribe link at the bottom of every such email does the same with no sign-in. Admins, Members and Guests never get the email and do not see the box.

sections.heading: Away
sections.text: Pick the first and the last day you are Away. While you are away, Prompts meant for you go to your Stand-in, and the Metric Owner and the Workflow's owner may enter a value for you (marked as entered by them; you are told through your Delivery Preference, and Quiet Hours hold the message). You can replace it with your own until the period is locked. The dates are saved as soon as both are set; Clear removes them. Owners and Admins can also set your Away dates on Members and Groups.

sections.heading: Heads-ups
sections.text: Under Heads-ups you choose whether Ziffr shows you the Heads-ups it notices and whether it also tells you by message. Show me Heads-ups under Analyze is on unless you turn it off; turning it off also stops the messages. Also tell me by message is off until you turn it on. Then the strongest Heads-ups you were not told yet reach you by your Delivery Preference for replies and updates, at most 3 in any 7 days, each once (one that ended and came back can be sent again). Quiet hours hold them like an Alert, and one is not sent after you lose sight of either of its Metrics. A message cannot be…

sections.heading: Quiet hours
sections.text:
Under Quiet hours you choose the hours of the night and the whole days (the weekend, say) when Ziffr should leave you alone: from 19:00 until 07:00, and all day Saturday and Sunday. Requests for numbers, reminders, Alerts, Heads-ups and checklist items by message that would arrive then wait, and are sent when your quiet hours end; none is dropped. The times are in the time zone you pick there, or in the Workspace's. A Due Date does not move: only the message waits, so something due on Monday morning may be asked for first thing, when your quiet hours end.
If you set nothing, you follow the…

sections.heading: Send feedback
sections.text:
In the central version of Ziffr (ziffr.net), your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar has Send feedback. It opens a panel beside the page, so you can see what you are writing about. Choose what it is (A problem, An idea or A question), write your words (up to 2000 characters, with a counter under the box) and press Send feedback. You do not need an account anywhere else.
Read the note above the button before you send. Your words will be public on GitHub. Your name and your Workspace's data (Metric names, values and the like) are never sent. Ziffr adds only the page you are on, shortened to…

sections.heading: Answers to your feedback
sections.text: This is only in the central version of Ziffr (ziffr.net); a Ziffr that someone runs themselves has no feedback and sends nothing anywhere. When the Ziffr team answers the post that was made from your feedback, the answer is added under your feedback as a message from the Ziffr team, the feedback's status becomes answered, and Ziffr tells you the way it tells you about Tasks and Questions (in your own Connector, within your Quiet Hours, at most once an hour for one feedback). The message only says that there is an answer, and its link opens My feedback in the panel. Choose a feedback in the…

sections.heading: The question about Ziffr
sections.text: Now and then, where an Installation Admin has turned it on (hosted Ziffr does), a small card in the corner asks whether you like Ziffr. Yes offers a link to the Ziffr repository on GitHub, where you can star it if you want to; Ziffr tells GitHub nothing about you. Not yet asks what is missing, and your words go to the people who run this Ziffr without your name. Not now closes it, and it comes back after 30 days, then once more after 60; Don't ask again ends it. It never appears while you are looking at a form, in the demo, or on a shared View Link.

sections.heading: Your Alerts
sections.text: Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar, or from Alerts in the settings area. An Alert is your own standing request to be told when a Metric you see reaches a level; you set one with Alert me… on the Metric's page (see The Metrics screens). This page lists every Alert you hold in the current Workspace on a Metric you can still see, with its condition, the way it is delivered, and where it stands: waiting, fired (quiet until the condition has been false again) and when it last fired. The page says the limits: the Alerts you may hold in a Workspace (20 unless the Workspace or…

sections.heading: Connected assistants
sections.text: You → Connected assistants lists the AI assistants you connected to Ziffr by its address, such as Claude.ai: for each, the name it gave itself, the Workspace, what it may do, when you connected it, when it was last used and until when it works. Disconnect ends one at once. A connection also ends on its end date and when you leave its Workspace, and an Owner can end it on the Workspace's Access Keys page, where it shows as a Connected assistant.

sections.heading: Connecting an assistant
sections.text:
Connected assistants also shows how to connect one: the address to add in Claude.ai and other assistants on the web, and the lines for Claude Code and Claude Desktop with an Access Key. Connectors only points here.
In the assistant, add a connector with your Ziffr's address followed by /mcp, such as https://ziffr.example.com/mcp. The page shows the exact address. The assistant opens Ziffr's page Connect an assistant to Ziffr?, after you sign in if you are not signed in yet:
Without a Workspace of your own, the page says so: start one, then press Connect in the assistant again.
A connection…

sections.heading: Working with an assistant
sections.text:
Once Ziffr is connected, as in Connecting an assistant or with an Access Key on your own computer (An AI assistant), you ask the assistant in your own words. It looks things up in Ziffr and answers.
#### Ready-made requests
Ziffr offers the assistant a few Starters, ready-made requests you pick instead of writing them:
Where to find them:
Claude.ai and the Claude apps: press + in the message box and look under the connector's name, such as Ziffr. Pick a Starter, fill in what it asks for if you like, and send. Left empty, the assistant asks you.
Claude Code: type / and look for the commands…

sections.heading: Your Webhooks
sections.text: You → Your Webhooks lists the Personal Webhooks you added for yourself in this Workspace: an address outside Ziffr, such as your own n8n flow, that gets a signed message when something happens. Yours hears only what you may see here, checked at the moment it is sent, and acts as you: ticking a task off in your own list marks it done in Ziffr as you. Without the Workspace's switch the page says "Your Workspace does not allow personal Webhooks; ask an Owner or Admin" and shows none; an Owner or Admin switches it on under Workspace → Webhooks (Workspace settings). Owners, Admins and Members have…

sections.heading: Installation settings
sections.text:
This chapter is for the people who run a Ziffr for others: a team, a club or a company. If someone else runs your Ziffr, you never see this page, and you can skip it.
An Installation is one running Ziffr, with all its Workspaces. Its Installation Settings say what it talks to: the mail server, Telegram and Slack, and the check against bots. The people who may change them are its Installation Admins. Being an Owner of a Workspace does not make you one, and being one shows you nothing of anyone's Workspace.

sections.heading: Becoming the first Installation Admin
sections.text:
A new Ziffr has no Installation Admin. Until it has one, it writes a setup code to its server log each time it starts, such as K7Q2-M9XD-4HRT-BW3N.
1. Sign in to Ziffr.
2. Open /installation, for example https://ziffr.example.com/installation.
3. Copy the setup code from the server log. With Docker, docker compose logs app shows it. If it has left the log, opening the page writes a new one.
4. Enter it and choose Claim.
The code works once. After it, nobody can claim the Installation again, and the page answers "not found" to everyone who is not an Installation Admin. A wrong code is refused;…

sections.heading: Other Installation Admins
sections.text: Under Installation Admins, add someone by the email address they signed in with. They must have signed in to this Ziffr once before. Remove takes someone off the list, yourself included, but the last one stays: add another one first. People named on the server stay until the server's settings change.

sections.heading: Mail
sections.text:
Ziffr sends requests for values, reminders, replies and invitations by email once it has a mail server.
Mail server: the address of your SMTP server with its user and password, such as smtps://user:password@smtp.example.com:465.
Sender: the address emails come from, with a name if you like, such as Ziffr . Your mail server must be allowed to send as it.
Choose Save: it works at once, without restarting Ziffr. Then choose Send a test email to yourself. It goes to the address you signed in with, at most ten times an hour. If it fails, the page says one of: could not reach the mail server, the…

sections.heading: Replies by email
sections.text:
People can answer a request for a value, a question or a task by replying to its email, once mail works and replies are set up. Replies go to a domain of their own, such as in.ziffr.example.com; your inbound mail provider takes them and forwards each one to Ziffr, signed.
Domain for replies: the domain replies go to.
Signing secret: signs what the provider forwards. Choose Make a signing secret: the page shows a new one once, with Copy, for your provider's forwarder. It never shows it again; Make a new signing secret replaces it, and the old one stops working at once.
Provider that vouches…

sections.heading: Telegram
sections.text:
Ziffr asks for values and takes the answers by Telegram once it has a bot. One bot serves the whole Installation; each Workspace then turns Telegram on for itself on its Connectors page.
1. In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, and give the bot a name and a username ending in bot.
2. Copy the token BotFather sends, such as 7000000001:AAF…. Whoever has it can send and read as the bot, so keep it to yourself.
3. Paste it under Bot token and choose Save.
4. Optional: under the form, download it gives a picture for the bot. In @BotFather send /setuserpic, choose the bot and send the…

sections.heading: Slack
sections.text:
Ziffr sends requests for values to people's Slack and takes their answers once the Installation has a Slack app. One app serves the whole Installation; each Workspace then connects its own Slack workspace on its Connectors page.
1. Choose Create the Slack app. Slack opens with Ziffr's manifest already filled in for this Ziffr's address. Pick the Slack workspace that owns the app and choose Create. If the page says Slack only talks to an https address, whoever runs the server sets this Ziffr's https address there first. Download the Slack app icon, below the steps, gives the picture to upload…

sections.heading: Workspace Limits
sections.text:
A Workspace Limit is the most Metrics a Workspace may hold. Archived Metrics do not count; Derived Metrics do. Without a default and without a limit of its own, a Workspace has no limit, which is how most Installations run.
Default limit and Name of the default apply to every Workspace without a limit of its own, such as 10 and "Standard". Empty means no limit. "Working" next to the title means a default is set. The demo never has a limit, and a Trial Workspace keeps its own rule of 25 Metrics while it runs.
Workspaces lists every Workspace by name with how many Metrics it holds and its…

sections.heading: Sending limits
sections.text:
Every Workspace, person and API key has a daily or hourly ceiling on what it can send and store. They keep one Workspace or one program from using up your mail provider, the Telegram and Slack apps or your server. Each ceiling has a range and a normal value, shown under its field; leave a field empty to use the normal value. Each is also an environment variable named ZIFFRLIMIT..., and a value set on the server wins, as everywhere on this page.
Generated from the code, with the range each may be set to and its normal value (pnpm test fails when this table is out of date):
Alerts per person…

sections.heading: How long logs are kept
sections.text:
What is older than the days set here goes by itself; what is younger is never removed. A value outside its range is not used, and the usual one applies instead, so a typo can never shorten what is kept below the lowest allowed. The section says so when the server holds such a value.
Days the Audit Log is kept: 365 to 3,650, default 730 (two years). Below 730 the page warns in plain words: who did what back then can no longer be told. The Audit Log is never kept for fewer days than a Retention or an Approval still refers to: a Metric with a Retention, and a Metric with an open Approval, keep…

sections.heading: Marketplace
sections.text:
The Marketplace lists Packs others made: ready-made Metric Catalog entries, templates, designs and Themes. The connection is off unless you turn it on; without it, Owners and Admins install Packs from a file.
Connection: on or off. "Working" next to the title means it is on and its address is accepted.
Marketplace address: empty for Ziffr's own. It starts with https://, has no user or ? part, and is never inside this server's own network (unless the server allows it with ZIFFRALLOWPRIVATEMARKETPLACE=1).
With it on, this server, never a browser, asks the Marketplace for lists of Packs, a…

sections.heading: Set on the server
sections.text:
A setting your server's settings file already has wins over the page. The page then shows it as Set on the server, and it can be changed only there. Nothing changes for a Ziffr that was set up with a file.
On a Ziffr Cloud deployment (hosted Ziffr), the Workspace Limits, the days over the limit, the days a trial lasts and its data stays, and the wait before an unused Workspace goes are fixed by Ziffr Cloud. The page shows them as Set by Ziffr Cloud and changes none of them, nor the limit of a single Workspace; only Ziffr Cloud sets those. Every log and capacity setting stays yours.

sections.heading: Check against bots
sections.text:
A Ziffr that strangers can reach should check that whoever asks for a sign-in link is a person: otherwise a program could make it email any address. Ziffr uses Cloudflare Turnstile.
1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, under Turnstile, choose Add widget, add this Ziffr's domain, and pick the mode Managed.
2. Copy the widget's Site key and Secret key into the two fields and choose Save.
Ziffr asks Cloudflare whether it knows the secret key first and saves nothing Cloudflare does not know, so a wrong key never shuts everyone out of signing in. Once both are saved, the section says "Working", and the…

sections.heading: Trials
sections.text:
Trials are something hosted Ziffr offers, so this section exists only on a Ziffr Cloud deployment. On any other Ziffr the page has no Trials section, the sign-in page has no trial, and every Workspace made here is an ordinary one. If the server's settings file, or a Trials section saved by an older version, still sets the trial days, no Workspace can be made until that is removed.
On hosted Ziffr this section holds what happens when a trial ends and whether trials may have Webhooks. The numbers that bound a trial are in the next section.

sections.heading: Trial Limits
sections.text:
Like Trials, this section exists only on hosted Ziffr. It lists the Trial Limits, the numbers that bound every trial, each with its range:
Days a trial lasts (1 to 30; empty: 14). Applies to trials made afterwards.
Days a trial's data stays after it ends (1 to 60; empty: 7).
Trials at once (1 to 100,000; empty: 500).
People in a trial (1 to 25; empty: 5). Members, Admins and Guests, the Owner and the invitations that are still open included.
Invitation emails a trial sends a day (0 to 50; empty: 10). Resends count; 0 means trials send none.
Invitation emails all trials send a day (0 to 5,000;…

sections.heading: Usage
sections.text:
The Usage section shows what this Installation is used for, as daily counts: how many Workspaces and people there are, how many Metrics, dashboards and decks, how many values arrived by each Source, how many calls programs made and how often dashboards, decks and Metrics were opened. It never shows a Workspace's or a Metric's name, a person or a value, and nothing is sent anywhere. Ziffr counts each day at 04:40 UTC, for the day before, so a new Installation shows figures from its second day.
How each figure is counted. Calls (apicalls, feedcalls, mcpcalls) are counted in memory by each…

sections.heading: Encryption
sections.text:
Every Workspace has a Workspace Key of its own, kept only wrapped under this Installation's ZIFFRSECRETSKEY, and Ziffr seals the words people write, its Contacts' details and the Outbox, the intake log and the Audit Log with it. Rows written before an upgrade are in clear until a job seals them, a few hundred at a time, every five minutes; nothing stops while it runs. The Encryption of Workspaces section shows how far it is.
At the top, how many Workspaces are fully encrypted and have a key, how many values are still in clear and how many are moving to a newer key version. Without…

sections.heading: Demo
sections.text: Offer the demo decides whether the sign-in page has Try the demo: Offered on the login page or Not offered. A Ziffr run with Docker on a domain has the demo off on the server, where the page shows it as set on the server; the person who runs it offers the demo there in the server's settings file. On a laptop the demo is offered unless you choose otherwise here. The section says whether the sign-in page offers it. A Ziffr that is a public demo and nothing else is set so on the server; the section then says so, and nobody signs in there. Visitors may change the demo (off by default) is for that…

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.text:
Ask people whether they like Ziffr decides whether signed-in people see a small card now and then: "Enjoying Ziffr?". Choose Ask now and then or Never ask; empty means on for hosted Ziffr and off everywhere else.
The card shows only to Owners, Admins and Members who have submitted values on at least 3 different days, never in the demo, to Guests or on a View Link, and at most three times for each person: the second time after 30 days, the third after 60 more. Nobody sees it again after choosing Star on GitHub or Don't ask again. A yes opens the Ziffr repository on GitHub, where the person…

sections.heading: Changes
sections.text: Changes lists who changed what, and when: claiming, adding and removing Installation Admins, saving or removing a setting such as the mail server, the replies signing secret, the Turnstile secret key, trials, the demo, the Telegram bot token or the Slack Client Secret, a Workspace's limit, test emails and replies tests. It names the setting, never its value. When Ziffr deletes a Workspace, such as a trial that ended, it shows one line by Ziffr with the Workspace's id, never its name, at the moment it destroys the Workspace's key, the first step of the deletion. What is left of it in the…

sections.heading: Packs
sections.text: A Pack is a file of ready-made things for a Workspace: Metric Catalog entries, Dashboard and Deck Templates, Workflow Templates, View Designs, Analysis Recipes and Themes. It holds no code. Open Workspace → Packs.

sections.heading: The installed Packs
sections.text:
Installed in this Workspace lists each Pack with its version, author and license, whether it was an uploaded file, when and by whom it was installed, and what it added: its Metric Catalog entries, templates, designs and Themes. A Pack's own page and help page open as plain links, when it has them; for a Pack that came as a file, not from the Marketplace, the link names its site and says the Marketplace did not check it. Owners, Admins and Members see the list; Guests see no Packs.
Each Pack shows "by" its author, with its logo when it has one, in a bordered box next to the name, and says who…

sections.heading: Ziffr's own Packs
sections.text:
Ziffr's own Packs lists the twelve Packs that come with this version of Ziffr, for Owners and Admins. Each shows its name, version and summary and what it brings as counts (for example "13 Metrics, 2 dashboards, 2 Workflows"). It works on any Installation, also a self-hosted one with no Marketplace: nothing is downloaded and nothing leaves your server.
Choose Preview with Sample Data to see everything the Pack adds, drawn with Sample Data and never your own values. These Packs need no confirmation about where they came from; texts aimed at assistants, if one ever had any, would still be…

sections.heading: Installing from a file
sections.text:
Ziffr makes starting Packs: SaaS metrics, Online shop, Agency or freelancer, Sports club and a Board meeting deck, and five for the functions of a business that any company can use: Sales, Finance, People and HR, Customer support, and Operations and fulfilment. Each brings its Metrics, a dashboard and a Workflow, and names the ready n8n templates that can fill them. They come with Ziffr: install one from Ziffr's own Packs, below, with no download. Their files are also in the packs folder of Ziffr's repository, to read or to install as a file.
SaaS metrics is the fullest: 13 Metrics with Tags,…

sections.heading: Set up from this Pack
sections.text:
Installing adds only entries and templates. Set up from this Pack, under an installed Pack, turns them into things you use. It is for Owners and Admins.
The form opens with the whole Pack chosen: every Metric ticked, the dashboard and the Workflow picked when the Pack has exactly one of each, and, when you are the only member of the Workspace, you as the Approver when its Approve step asks for just one. Press Set up to take it all, or untick and change what you do not want. When the Workspace has other members, Approvers start empty: you pick them.
When Set up has made Metrics that take…

sections.heading: From the Marketplace
sections.text: When an Installation Admin turned on the Marketplace connection, Owners and Admins see From the Marketplace: search free Packs by a word, and choose See what it adds to see one drawn with Sample Data. A Pack from the Marketplace says so ("its signature holds") and needs no warning about where it came from; texts aimed at assistants are still listed and need a tick. Installing works as from a file. Once a day Ziffr asks which installed Packs have newer versions; an installed Pack with one shows Version … on the Marketplace…, which shows what an update changes before it is done.

sections.heading: Updating a Pack
Uninstalling a Pack
sections.text: Uninstall… first lists what goes and what stays. It removes every item nobody changed and nothing uses. It keeps, no longer marked as from the Pack, every item you changed and every Theme a dashboard, a deck or the Workspace's default uses. Metrics made from its catalog entries, and everything else made from the Pack, stay as they are. When a kept Theme still shows the Pack's logo, the window says so and offers Also remove the author's logo from this Theme, ticked by default: the Pack that brought the logo is gone. A logo you chose yourself always stays. The Audit log records it, with how…

sections.heading: Export as Pack
sections.text: Export as Pack… is for everyone but Guests. Pick Metrics, Metric Catalog entries from Packs, Dashboard, Deck and Workflow Templates, View Designs and Themes; name the Pack, give it an id such as northwind/saas-metrics, a version, a summary, an author and a license; then choose Download Pack. The file holds descriptions and layouts, never a value or a person, and only Metrics you see. Tags of the Metrics you pick go in too, up to 5 per entry and only Tags you see on those Metrics, never a Tag of a Metric you did not pick; untick Carry the Tags of the Metrics you pick to leave them out.…

sections.heading: Words in Ziffr

Every word Ziffr uses, and what it means. The app, this guide and the people who build Ziffr all use these words in the same way, so a word here means the same thing on every screen.
Some entries end with "Elsewhere you may see": words other tools use for something similar. Ziffr does not use them, because they usually mean something slightly different. If you are used to a "KPI", look up Metric.
Throughout the guide, a term in bold leads to its entry here.
